expects.rule: The first screen or the header gives the address, today's opening hours and a way to book or call, as text.
The menu is real text with prices, readable on a phone and by a screen reader, not only a PDF or an image.
The phone number is a tap-to-call link and the address opens a map.
Booking is one clear button that stays reachable while scrolling, and the site says when no booking is needed.
Special hours (holidays, closed days, kitchen last order) are stated in the same place as the regular hours.
Photographs show the real room, food and people of the place, and weigh little enough to load fast on mobile data.
Allergen and dietary information is available from the menu.
Opening hours, address, phone and a menu link are also published as LocalBusiness structured data, so search results can show them.

traits: 6 of 8 put a photograph or full-bleed image on most of the first screen (Delice, Ballena, Madie, 11 Bar, The Devonshire, Le Petit Bleu); the two others use a logo or an illustration.
A booking or ordering button is visible on the first screen of 6 of 8 (Delice, Studenterkilden, Ballena, 11 Bar, The Devonshire, Le Petit Bleu), as a labelled button, not an icon alone.
Hours or an open-now line appear on the first screen of only 2 of 8 (Delice's top strip, Le Petit Bleu); on the others they are lower down or in the footer, as text.
4 of 8 put an intro, pop-up or splash over the first screen on load (Studenterkilden, Ballena, The Devonshire, Le Petit Bleu): a cost to check against the point of the page.
The page background is cream or off-white on 7 of 8 (#f6efe6 to #fff7d7, or #fdfdfd); one is black. Colour comes from the venue and its photographs, with one accent.
1 of 8 uses one typeface; 5 of 8 pair a display face for the headline with a plain face for details; the three or four faces on Madie and TAB are a brand choice, not a rule.
First-screen text is short: under 40 words on 5 of 8 (Studenterkilden, Ballena, 11 Bar, TAB, Devonshire without its pop-up); Delice and Le Petit Bleu carry more because they list offers.

sites.name: Delice (Levis)

Set in Filson Soft and Ivy Mode.

avoid: Menu only as a PDF or an image: it cannot be read on a phone or by a screen reader.
Hours, address and phone only inside a hero video or an image, or only in the footer.
A pop-up (newsletter, banner) covering the first screen before the visitor sees the hours.
A site that asks the visitor to rotate the device to see it.
Stock photographs of generic dishes instead of the real place.
A reservation widget that only opens a third-party page with no phone number as a fallback.
A placeholder page that still says 'coming soon' after the opening date.
